newsitem.title: CROATIA: Blazing Croat resort isle calls state of emergency.
newsitem.headline: Blazing Croat resort isle calls state of emergency.

text.p: Firefighters struggled to contain a huge forest fire on the Croatian resort island of Hvar and authorities have imposed a state of emergency in the popular Adriatic holiday destination, state radio said on Tuesday.
The flames, whipped by strong winds, had swallowed almost 1,500 hectares (3,700 Acres) of pine forest, brush and lavender fields since the fire broke out around midday on Monday, it said.
"The fire has not yet been brought under control although we are doing what we can to contain it," a police official in the town of Hvar told Reuters by telephone.

"It spread from the centre of the island to the south overnight due to northern 'Tramuntana' wind," he said. "The direction of the wind has now changed to south-westerly but it is still keeping the fire alive."
Several of the 500 firemen were said to have sustained minor injuries in the morning.
Army units, three planes and two helicopters had been called in to help fight the fire, police said.
The scenic old town of Hvar and nearby islet of Ris were left without electricity. The authorities also closed Hvar's main road to allow the quick passage of water tankers.
Listed on tourist maps as Croatia's sunniest island, Hvar is one of the favourite tourist destinations on the coast.
